The Prophet says we would doubt sooner than Abraham, who asked to see the dead revived; he asks mercy on Lot, and would have accepted release after Joseph's long imprisonment.
The Prophet asks Allah's mercy on Lot, who wanted powerful support, and says that after a stay in prison as long as Joseph's he would have accepted release.
Aisha explains verse 12.110: the apostles despaired of their disbelieving nations and feared even their followers wavered, never doubting their Lord, until Allah's help came.
Picking Arak fruit, the Prophet says the black ones are best, and when asked if he had been a shepherd, says every prophet was one.
Ibn Abbas read 'kudhibu' in the verse on messengers losing hope, but Aisha read 'kudh-dhibu', saying the messengers feared their followers would call them liars, never doubting Allah's promise.
Aisha explained that the messengers despaired of their disbelieving people and thought their followers called them liars, never suspecting that Allah had betrayed them.
Gathering kabath fruit, the Prophet said the black ones are better, and when asked if he had shepherded sheep, said every prophet had done so.
